issue.title: Reuse one cargo target across an agent session's turns so verify cycles build incrementally

task_type_fields.proposal:
Reuse one cargo target directory across an agent session's turns, so that each
LLM turn -> `just check` monitor cycle in a Rust project rebuilds incrementally
instead of compiling a fresh ~2.5 GB target from scratch.

Today `spawn_agent_subprocess` (src/sase/agent/launch_spawn.py) mints a new
launch scratch key for every launch and points CARGO_TARGET_DIR at
`~/.cache/sase/tmp/cargo-targets/<key>`. The monitored command inherits the
starter's env, so every verify cycle starts from an empty target. Epic sase-1n8
(phase sase-1n8.4, commits 25d14fae6c and 379040e699) now reclaims the starter's
cargo target when its monitor settles. That bounds the disk footprint to about
one launch-sized target, but each cycle still pays a full cold build (5-7 min
per `just check` in the bob-cli-a0.5.1.5 incident).

A design has to answer:
- which key a session shares: the agent session, or the first member's key;
- how liveness and ownership work when several members or monitors could hold
  the dir at once;
- how monitor-settlement reclaim (proc_adapter._cleanup_starter_cargo_target)
  and the managed_tmp_reap dead-launch backstop decide that a shared target is
  finally unheld.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope:
Proposed by phase sase-1n8.4 (note #3) and named out of scope in the sase-1n8
plan (Phase 4: "Reusing one cargo target across an agent session's turns ... is
a separate performance follow-up and out of scope"). sase-1n8 fixed the disk
churn by reclaiming each starter's target. Sharing a target across turns is a
build-performance change with its own ownership and liveness design.

issue.creation_reason: Filed by the sase-1n8 land agent from PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP sase-1n8.4 note #3. The epic plan explicitly scoped cross-turn cargo-target reuse out and asked for a task bead if none existed; searches found none.

payload.description: Epic whose phase sase-1n8.4 added monitor-settlement reclaim of the starter cargo target; a shared target must cooperate with that reclaim
